plan: v9: v7-full pipeline with a symmetric altitude term in the score (bench10)
written: 2026-10-20 ~23:20 JST, before any v9 episode; v7 full (M3 2/5) and v8 (M4 0/5) verdicts stand unchanged
motivation_disclosed: Proposed after the v8 analysis: 5 of the 10 SNN + ES crashes in v8 were upward height escapes after the manoeuvre. Re-flying them showed the learned layer handing back at about +41 cm and climbing at about +40 cm/s (classical: about -5 cm, -6 cm/s); learned motor pulses add lift, the learned layer does not observe height, and bench9 scored altitude LOSS only (0.03 per cm below the start), so climbing was free. v9 closes that gap in the score for every arm.
score: bench10.score10 = bench9 score − 0.03·(altitude loss cm) + 0.03·(max |z − z(t0)| cm from the command onset to the end of the episode). Same weight as the old loss term; tasks, windows, crash definition and all other terms unchanged.
crash: unchanged: tilt > 80.2°, |z − z_start| > 1 m (height escape, up or down), z < 0.12 m, numerical

controllers.snn_es: descend9 imitation starts s1–s5 (identical files to v7 full) + careful ES (lr 0.01, sigma 0.02, pop 16, 4 cases per task per generation, 20 generations, every generation saved) with the descend9 objective on bench10 scores
controllers.opponents: bench9 classical schedules (plan_v7 pilot9.json), normalisers recomputed with bench10 scoring on 24 training cases per task

selection.rule: 0 crashes and tilt < 70 deg on all 96; lowest objective

primary_M4.per_seed: average ratio <= 0.95 AND crashed episodes <= classical crashed episodes on the same 192 cases

secondary: snn_bc (imitation starts) on the same blind set
